title: A Parisian Night in Istanbul: Olivier Giraud Brings His Hit English-Language Comedy to Ataşehir
excerpt: French comedian Olivier Giraud performs How to Become a Parisian in One Hour? — fully in English — at DasDas Sahne on Saturday, October 24. Here's who he is, what to expect, and how to save 300 TL.
bodyHtml:
The French comedian performs How to Become a Parisian in One Hour? at DasDas Sahne on Saturday, October 24, with an advertised 300 TL discount.

Ever been glared at by a waiter, scolded at a shop counter, or left wondering whether you broke an unwritten rule? Then you're halfway to becoming a Parisian. Olivier Giraud will happily teach you the rest.

On Saturday, October 24, 2026, the French comedian brings his long-running hit How to Become a Parisian in One Hour? to DasDas Sahne in Ataşehir. The show is performed entirely in English, with no subtitles or translation. That makes it an easy night out for expats, international students and English-speaking locals.

Meet the comedian

Olivier Giraud grew up in Bordeaux and first came to Paris to train as a chef. He then worked in the hotel business, including a stint living abroad. That time away made him notice how differently Americans and the French go about everyday life, and those observations became his material.

He was told an all-English comedy show could never work in Paris. He launched it anyway in 2009, through a production company he cheekily named French Arrogance Prod. More than fifteen years later, the show is still running at the 600-seat Théâtre des Nouveautés in Paris. It has also toured to cities including London and Brussels. According to the show, more than 800,000 people have now seen it.

Parisian life, with a comic twist

The show is a series of "lessons" in behaving like a true Parisian. You'll learn how to act in restaurants, shops, taxis and the metro, and above all how to master the famous Parisian attitude. Giraud plays it all for laughs: the impatience, the raised eyebrows, the pursed lips and the legendary arrogance.

The show is interactive, so the audience becomes part of it. You don't need to speak French, know Paris or understand its unwritten rules to enjoy it.

Why it lands for expats

Anyone who has moved to a new country knows the feeling of learning a culture's rules as they go, usually by getting them wrong first. Giraud's humour comes from exactly that culture clash. For an international crowd in Istanbul, it should feel very familiar.

Make an evening of it: invite a friend, meet for dinner beforehand and let Giraud handle the introduction to Parisian manners.

Save 300 TL with PARIS2026

The advertised offer lists tickets at 1,200 TL instead of 1,500 TL with promo code PARIS2026. Enter the code when booking, and check that the discount appears before you complete payment.
